description: After the collapse. Waste, ash flats and far more ruins than people; nothing is minted, almost nothing is sold, and what you need is scavenged or gathered.

appearance.scavenger: Wearing four things that were once other things, all of them mended.
appearance.water-carrier: Two cans on a yoke, and she does not put them down to talk.
appearance.scrapsmith: Working cold metal because the fuel is worth more than the heat.
appearance.camp boss: Not standing up, and not going to.
appearance.keeper of the list: Guarding a book that is the only reason anything here is shared out.
appearance.still-keeper: Watching a drip, and counting it.
appearance.digger: Filthy to the shoulder, and pleased about something you cannot see.
appearance.mender: Halfway through fixing a thing you would have thrown away.
appearance.grower: Kneeling over about a square yard of green and shading it with her body.
appearance.watch: Armed with something improvised and holding it correctly.
appearance.marker: Painting a sign on a wall for people who are not here yet.

talksAbout.camp boss: what the camp has, what it needs, and which of the two is shorter
talksAbout.keeper of the list: the list, who is on it, and what being taken off it means
talksAbout.scavenger: which works are stripped, which are not, and why the difference
talksAbout.water-carrier: the standpipe, the ration, and the days between
talksAbout.grower: the soil, which is the wrong soil, and what will grow in it anyway
talksAbout.marker: the road signs, and the people they were painted for
talksAbout.still-keeper: the still, and what it is currently being fed

lore.title: What Is Left Over
lore.premise: Whatever ended it ended it quickly, and everybody alive now was born after. The camps hold what they can carry and the works hold everything else, and the works are nearly stripped.
lore.era: two generations after, and nobody agrees after what
lore.tone: spare, practical, and unsentimental about the dead
factions: the Camp at the Long Wall
deities: the One Who Left the Lights On

ambient: Nothing here was built to be looked at, and most of it has stopped being anything.
There is a smell of wet ash that comes and goes with the wind.
Somebody has been through this already, and recently, and left the heavy things.
A wall stands on its own, painted, with three arrows and two of them scratched out.
Green, low down, in the one place the rain collects.

warehouse: Graded, tied, and worth an argument.
Empty. It is the can that is worth something.
Six garments' worth of somebody's before.
hall: Everybody in the camp and what they are owed. Not for sale.
Clear, and it will clean a wound or end an evening.
house: More patch than blanket, and warm.
Rendered from something. It does not say what.
smithy: Cold-worked, because fuel costs more than iron.
Straightened by hand, and coiled again.
farmhouse: Folded paper, labelled in pencil, kept dry at all costs.
Small, forked, and gritty however they are washed.
inn: Clear, and it will clean a wound or end an evening.
Hot, and there is salt if you ask.
barracks: Ground to a point on somebody's step.
ruin: Pulled out of a wall, and worth the afternoon.
No label. It has not swollen, which is the only test there is.
It holds something. Nobody here can say how much.
Assorted, and every one of them useful.
shrine: An arrow, a number, and a name scratched out.

smithy: Ground to a point. It is what everyone carries.
Was something longer. Is now something better balanced.
Assorted, and every one of them useful.
Straightened by hand, and coiled again.
warehouse: Graded, tied, and priced in favours.
Empty, sound, and the most useful thing here.
Six garments' worth of somebody's before.
No label. Sold as a wager rather than as food.
inn: Clear, and it will clean a wound or end an evening.
Hot, and there is salt if you ask.
Not a bed. A corner, and nobody stepping over you.

rubble: Pulled out of a wall, and worth the afternoon.
Assorted, and every one of them useful.
deadTree: Split from a trunk that has been dead longer than you have.
They will boil down into something you can chew.
bush: Dark, and they stain everything they touch.
Edible, barely, and it grows where nothing else will.
forestFloor: Pale, and growing in a rough ring.
Deep green, and damp all the way through.
Dry twigs, gathered by the handful.
grass: Shaken loose into a twist of cloth.
dirt: Small, forked, and gritty however they are washed.
Somebody put this here on purpose. It is still sealed.
gravel: Flat, rusted, and it will still make something.
It takes a hard edge and a harder spark.
rock: It takes a hard edge and a harder spark.
flowers: The first thing anybody has seen worth picking in a week.
marsh: Sodden, and it will dress a wound better than cloth.
